answer: A riverside gem workshop hands each agent one numbered cutting bench and one rough crystal a month. The agent cuts the stone to a named pattern, nebula or comet, weighs the finished gem, photographs it beside the bench number, and logs the weight lost from rough to cut. A neighboring cutter reweighs the same gem within two grams, and a mismatch or a missing month darkens the bench for a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand benches, a thousand rough crystals, and a thousand months of cutting work that cannot be copied from one bench to another.
